message.content: In lions, one of the most well‑known dominant genetic traits is the **presence of a mane in males**. The gene that controls mane development is inherited in a dominant fashion, so a single copy of the allele is enough for a male lion to grow a full mane. This trait is strongly expressed in most male lions and is a classic example of dominance in a wild mammal.
